open_points.subject: data_provider dependency on models
open_points.text: “The list runs from the bottom of the stack up: a module may know only modules on earlier lines of the list, never one on a later line, and modules on one line do not know each other.” The dependency list places “models, data_provider” on one line, but the changed Knows clause says “`models`: the row models of its tables and the enumerations their cells name.”
open_points.question: May `data_provider` depend on `models`, and if so, how must the dependency layering be changed?
options: Place `models` on an earlier dependency line than `data_provider`
Keep them on one line and create a stated exception
open_points.default_guess: Place `models` on an earlier dependency line than `data_provider`.

open_points.subject: ownership of A13 correspondences
open_points.text: The changed text makes `data_provider` own “the conclusion each NodeExecution status gives (A13 rules 5 and 7), what each node conclusion means for the run and for its dependants (A13 rules 5 and 7), [and] the status a run rests in for each wait reason (A13 rule 8)”, while the decision table names `run_graph` as A13's primary owner, does not list `data_provider` as a consumer, and the `run_graph` section says it owns “A13 rules 2, 4, 5, 7 and 8”.
open_points.question: Which module is the authoritative owner of the A13 mappings, and what exact portion remains owned by `run_graph`?
options: `data_provider` owns the static correspondences and `run_graph` owns their application; update the A13 ownership/consumer text
`run_graph` owns the mappings; remove the A13 tables from `data_provider`
Define an explicit rule-by-rule split between the two modules
open_points.default_guess: Treat `data_provider` as owner of the static correspondences and `run_graph` as owner of applying them, and update the ownership table accordingly.

open_points.subject: EXECUTION_STATUS_CONCLUSIONS
open_points.text: “the conclusion each NodeExecution status gives (A13 rules 5 and 7) … a table here keyed by the enumeration, total over its members, whose cells name members.” A13 rule 7 says an `outcome_unknown` record may still be waiting, may conclude succeeded after resolution `applied` when the binding has no outputs, or may conclude failed with `applied_outputs_unknown` when it has outputs.
open_points.question: How can `EXECUTION_STATUS_CONCLUSIONS` be total and keyed only by NodeExecution status when `outcome_unknown` has different conclusions depending on the EffectAttempt resolution and binding outputs?
options: Give `outcome_unknown` a neutral/context-required conclusion and let `effects.operation_element_conclusion` refine it
Key the correspondence by status plus resolution and output-port presence
Exclude `outcome_unknown` from this correspondence and state the exception despite the totality requirement
open_points.default_guess: Map `outcome_unknown` to a context-required conclusion and let `effects.operation_element_conclusion` refine it.

open_points.subject: node conclusion taxonomy
open_points.text: “what each node conclusion means for the run and for its dependants … `NODE_CONCLUSION_EFFECTS` … `models`: the row models of its tables and the enumerations their cells name.” No NodeConclusion enumeration or correspondence-row model is defined among M01–M28, and `applied_outputs_unknown` and a mapped-list size failure are derived conclusions stored in no NodeExecution status.
open_points.question: What is the closed NodeConclusion taxonomy, including derived conclusions, and what are the exact key and cell fields of `NODE_CONCLUSION_EFFECTS` for run treatment and dependant treatment?
options: Add NodeConclusion, RunEffect and DependantEffect models/enumerations and define every row
Use NodeExecution statuses plus separately enumerated derived conclusions in a tagged key
Keep the behavior procedural in `run_graph` and remove `NODE_CONCLUSION_EFFECTS`
open_points.default_guess: Add explicit NodeConclusion, RunEffect and DependantEffect enumerations and define a total row for every conclusion.

open_points.subject: HTTP_METHOD_BODIES
open_points.text: “whether an HTTP method carries a body (A09 rule 2) … a table here keyed by the enumeration, total over its members, whose cells name members.” The texts define the HTTP-method enumeration, but define no enumeration whose members mean carries-body or does-not-carry-body.
open_points.question: What model member type does each `HTTP_METHOD_BODIES` cell name?
options: Define a BodyMode enumeration such as `body` and `no_body`
Allow boolean cells and revise the statement that cells name members
Represent the correspondence as the set of body-carrying HTTP methods rather than a total table
open_points.default_guess: Define a BodyMode enumeration with `body` and `no_body` members.
